Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Evidence not fully researched in this subagent run. Eswatini participates in regional RTGS (SADC-RTGS) for cross-border settlements, and remittance channels exist, but I did not collect sufficient authoritative evidence on cross-border instant/retail interoperability status.

The AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 report (via Times of Eswatini, November 2025) confirms EPS Fast Payments, launched December 2024, is a domestic cross-domain instant payment system, and states this classification 'positions the kingdom for future integration into regional payment corridors' such as the SADC TCIB scheme. A 2025 World Bank financial sector assessment lists 'facilitating participation of PSPs in the SADC fast payments scheme (TCIB) and explor[ing] interlinking the EPS with the TCIB' among planned next steps — confirming cross-border instant functionality is at the planning stage only. revised_comments: Eswatini's instant payment system, the Eswatini Payment Switch (EPS) Fast Payments module, currently operates only domestically. Cross-border functionality is at the planning stage: the Central Bank of Eswatini and the World Bank have identified interlinking EPS with the SADC region's Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis (TCIB) scheme as a priority for future development, alongside continued participation in the SADC-RTGS wholesale settlement system for high-value cross-border flows. No live retail cross-border instant payment corridor is yet operational.

Comments: Evidence not fully researched in this subagent run. revision_notes: A light-touch check surfaced clear evidence, so the row was escalated to a full review with pages fetched and read. The Central Bank of Eswatini's Practice Note for Mobile Money Service Providers (in force from March 2019) contains a dedicated Consumer Protection section (clause 22) requiring disclosure of fees and charges, written customer agreements, functional dispute/complaints handling desks, free complaint hotlines, and data confidentiality obligations specific to mobile money/payment services. This is reinforced by the NPS Oversight Policy Framework's consumer protection and Ombudsman provisions and by the National Payment Systems Act 2023, which strengthens CBE's oversight of payment service providers including user protection. Value updated from 0/Unknown to 3/Yes.
revised_comments: Eswatini has dedicated regulatory provisions for digital payment consumer protection. The Central Bank of Eswatini's Practice Note for Mobile Money Service Providers (2019) requires disclosure of fees and charges, written customer agreements, functional complaints and dispute-resolution mechanisms, free customer hotlines, and confidentiality of customer data. These are reinforced by the National Payment & Settlement Systems Oversight Policy Framework, which includes consumer protection and Ombudsman provisions, and by the National Payment Systems Act 2023, which strengthens the Central Bank's oversight of payment service providers, including user protection.

An AFI-affiliated 2022 report on forcibly displaced persons (FDPs) in Eswatini documents that refugees and asylum-seekers are eligible for refugee ID or non-Swazi ID cards, and that several banks (Eswatini Bank, Standard Bank, Nedbank via its 'Ngeyakho' product) and MTN Eswatini mobile money accept refugee/non-Swazi documentation for account opening, generally with simplified due diligence, though MTN requires an Eswatini ID later and institutions apply risk-based discretion that can exclude higher-risk applicants. revised_comments: Refugees, asylum-seekers and other forcibly displaced persons (FDPs) in Eswatini can partially access digital payment accounts. FDPs are eligible for refugee or non-Swazi identity documents, which several commercial banks and MTN Eswatini's mobile money service accept for account opening, generally with simplified or risk-based due diligence, though access can be conditional (for example, MTN requires an Eswatini identity document after initial onboarding) and some institutions apply enhanced due diligence that can exclude higher-risk applicants. The Central Bank of Eswatini, working with the Commissioner for Refugees, has an active roadmap to formalise accepted KYC documentation for FDPs and to issue them a national personal identification number to broaden access to simplified due diligence financial products.
